ctx.x: And you got involved with your sisters.

And Eunice. And what they used to do, when we was in a concert, they would take me, and we'd learn some new steps... They'd take me for a guest at the Orpheum. See? The Orpheum used to have vaudeville, see. And in the ladies rooms, they'd change their clothes, see. And we would go in (?), and they'd say, "You all look good now." So we'd say, "All right." And then, "Have you got that step?" You'd say, "Yes." So we ran back in the ladies room and rehearse it! You see? Then we'd have a couple of new steps for the…

And it was called the Merry-Makers. And there were seventeen of us. We used to get three dollars for the concert. But actually my mother (?), because we'd have to wear new shoes and we had new dresses, and they'd be coming in the halls, you know, with these big dresses... Everybody had a big dress like they were (?) in New York or something! A great big dress, and after the concert was over, you got three dollars.
